rep.name: Richard Claessen
rep.location: Netherlands (originally Bulgaria; states he usually resides in Bulgaria)

prospect.name: Matteo M.
prospect.training_background: Trained hard in the gym 4-5x/week pre- and during COVID, then took roughly 2-3 years largely off and gained weight. Renewed gym membership end of March 2026 but attends on-off, one to two times a week. Has been working with a dietitian for about 11 months and has lost roughly 13 kg. Cites boredom with repetitive gym work as the reason attendance is inconsistent.
prospect.medical: No serious health issues or injuries reported. Upper-back tension attributed to height and desk-based sitting; sees a physiotherapist roughly once a month for manipulation and tension release. Self-rates flexibility 5/10.

signals: Diet already dialled in with a paid dietitian; explicitly frames the goal as refinement — 'more focus on having a healthy body, mobility' rather than rescue
Already down ~13 kg under his own steam before the call; wants the last 10% body fat and a mobility upgrade
Price landed slightly above expectation but produced no real resistance — 'It's a little bit more than what I was thinking about... we can work around that for sure'

Counter-signal for the_rebuilder: lost real ground across a 2-3 year lapse and is partway back; assigned the_optimizer because there is no expressed regret and the driver is boredom with his current modality, not recovering a former self

goals.text: Build a healthy body with a more pleasing aesthetic — not bodybuilder or model, just lean and functional
Drop roughly 10 percentage points of body fat, from a self-reported ~31% (BIA) toward 20-25%
Add muscle mass while holding bodyweight between 88 and 92 kg
Improve mobility and flexibility from a self-rated 5/10 to a 9 or 10, particularly given age and desk work
Train in a way that is engaging and entertaining enough that he actually keeps showing up as life gets busier
Train through primal/natural full-body movement rather than isolation work

pains.text: Gym workouts have become boring and repetitive; even the thought of going makes him skip sessions
Attendance is on-off — one or two sessions a week against an intended four to five
Lost 2-3 years of training entirely and gained weight during that lapse; says his body stores fat quickly when inactive even with the diet controlled
Upper-back tension from height plus sitting most of the day, managed with roughly monthly physiotherapy
Self-rates flexibility at 5/10 and says there is a lot of room for improvement
Does not know how to program or perform kettlebell work and expects to need form guidance

objections.raw_quote: It's a little bit more than what I was thinking about. It's not something like a figure to hear. So we can work around that for sure.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate, did not explore the gap, did not run the money play. Immediately treated it as a yes — 'Perfect. Amazing. Let's, let's get started then.' — and moved to booking.

objections.raw_quote: in terms of, you know, being carried or followed day by day, I don't think it's the case per person.
objections.rep_response: Reframed accountability away from hand-holding and toward form correction — asked whether he is 'someone that wants to make sure they're actually always doing the right thing' — which the prospect accepted.

offer.payment_plan_terms: 50% down and 50% later, agreed live at the prospect's prompting. No second-payment date, amount or schedule was stated on the call.

evidence: Payment link sent via chat and WhatsApp; prospect worked through a failed attempt on a UAE Mastercard and then reported 'Okay, it's processing now.'

Rep proceeded through full onboarding afterwards: Trevor onboarding call booked for Wednesday 19:15 local, agreement email sent, Skool community invite sent, onboarding questionnaire link sent on WhatsApp, plus a 30-day check-in booked for 23 July.

Counter-evidence: the transcript never contains an explicit payment-success confirmation. The rep says 'you should get two emails' and 'I think you don't, like, have access yet, right?' — Skool access was still pending at the end of the call.

Counter-evidence: the amount actually charged is ambiguous. The prospect asked 'Don't we say 50% down and 50% seconds?' and the rep agreed, so it is unclear whether $6,000 or $3,000 was collected on the call.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor on Wednesday at 19:15 CET; prospect to sign the agreement, join Skool and complete the onboarding questionnaire beforehand. Rep check-in booked 23 July at 18:00.

notable.note: Call was originally booked with Andrew Musial, who was pulled away; Richard covered it cold and closed it. The entire Consequence Frame phase was skipped and the deep-why line was abandoned after the prospect said 'It's, you know, doing for yourself' — the deal closed on modality appeal rather than on emotional leverage. The price objection was never isolated; the rep conceded a 50/50 split on the prospect's request without setting terms. Medical screening ('you've never had like a serious injury, right?') was asked only after the payment was already processing, as a leading question.

quality.notes: Severe and sustained. Whole passages are inverted: the block at 00:01:15 labelled 'Matteo M.' contains the rep's discovery questions ('did you say 92 or 98 kilos?'), and the long stretch from roughly 00:12:45 to 00:14:30 runs both sides under a single label. The 00:36:44-00:38:16 offer-transition block and the 00:50:48 injury question are also attributed to the wrong speaker. Role was read from content throughout; no line-level attribution was relied on.
